exemplars.title: AI Kitchen: Child-Readable Ingredient Labels and Transparency Stickers for Failure Anticipation and Reliance Calibration
exemplars.why: AI Kitchen adopts a coherent kitchen vocabulary—ingredient cards, recipes, testing, traps, and product stickers—and maps its familiar actions directly onto training-data selection, model testing, reliance practice, and transparency export.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above FusAIn because the evidence identifies several source-domain objects and actions alongside their corresponding AI operations, demonstrating the full structural signature rather than one especially clean mapping.

exemplars.title: FusAIn: Composing Generative AI Visual Prompts Using Pen-based Interaction
exemplars.why: FusAIn makes a familiar pen the prompt-composition surface: designers load it with objects or visual attributes such as color and texture, turning the physical logic of preparing and using drawing tools into operations over a generative specification.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above PromptPaint because its quotation states the actionable correspondence—loading a pen with particular prompt payloads—more concretely than PromptPaint states how individual paint-like interactions translate into generation controls.

exemplars.title: PromptPaint: Steering Text-to-Image Generation Through Paint Medium-like Interactions
exemplars.why: PromptPaint uses paint-medium interactions as the direct steering surface for diffusion-based image generation, replacing model-specific parameter controls with an established vocabulary of artistic media and manipulation.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above SwipeGANSpace because the evidence explicitly says the borrowed interaction vocabulary steers generation, whereas SwipeGANSpace’s quotation establishes the matchmaking-inspired presentation but not what each swipe does to latent-space exploration.

notes: I departed from the consensus by placing AI Kitchen first and FusAIn second, ahead of PromptPaint. The adjustment reflects structural evidence: AI Kitchen enumerates multiple metaphor-to-system correspondences, while FusAIn gives the clearest single action-to-operation mapping. PromptPaint remains selected because the borrowed painting interaction is explicitly the steering mechanism, but its score is reduced because the evidence names media such as oil and watercolor without specifying individual gestures or their system effects. No score differs from the consensus by more than 0.3. Readers should treat all three mappings as supported by very short abstract/figure excerpts rather than complete interaction descriptions; AI Kitchen’s quote is broad but does not prove every kitchen term has a strict one-to-one system correspondence, and PromptPaint is especially underspecified at that level.
